item.title: Takayama Festival Float Museum: See the Ornate Festival Yatai Year-Round — Guide
item.description: The Takayama Festival’s elaborate wooden yatai floats, considered masterworks of Hida carpentry decorated with gilding, intricate carvings, lacquer and mechanical marionettes, only appear on the streets during the twice-yearly festival, but the Takayama Festival Float Museum (Yatai Kaikan) lets visitors see several of them up close throughout the year. Displayed in a hall beside the Sakurayama Hachimangu shrine, the rotating selection of towering floats offers a rare chance to appreciate the extraordinary craftsmanship in detail, whatever season you visit.

item.title: Fukuoka Food Guide: Hakata Ramen, Mentaiko, Yatai Stalls & More
item.description: Fukuoka is Japan’s greatest food city for its size. In a city of 1.6 million people, the density of excellent, affordable, deeply regional food is extraordinary — from the tonkotsu ramen counters that fill at midnight to the yatai open-air stalls on the Nakasu riverfront, from the morning fresh tuna market at Yanagibashi to the mentaiko tasting counters at Hakata Station. Fukuoka’s food identity is the food of Hakata (the old merchant district of the city): direct, unpretentious, built around pork offal, rich broth, and fermented seafood.
